biggest_catch: Payment is only for people who pass prescreening AND are found eligible for the main study visit — females aged 28 to 40, in person at Colorado State University — and 'up to $125' is a ceiling, not a guarantee.
catches: Not everyone qualifies: only females aged 28 to 40, and only those found eligible for the main part of the study are paid — prescreening and the screening visit are gates.

'Up to $125' is a ceiling, not a guaranteed amount; payment is stated only for those found eligible for the main part of the study — no payment is described for prescreening or the screening visit alone.

Medical procedures involved: blood draws and a bone mineral density/body composition scan (non-invasive imaging), plus non-invasive vascular tests and cognitive testing — ask the study team about any procedure-related risks at informed consent.
In-person visits at Colorado State University; the visits are spread across roughly two months, so regional access matters.
You also receive some of your test results from the study procedures; follow up with your own doctor with any health concerns.

steps: Confirm you are a female aged 28 to 40 interested in a heart and brain health study at Colorado State University's Department of Health and Exercise Science.
Complete the online prescreening survey linked from the official CSU announcement page.
If prescreened as potentially eligible, attend the consent/screening visit (about 90 minutes) at the CSU research site.

If found eligible for the main part of the study, attend the main study visit (about three and a half hours): blood pressure screening, blood draws, non-invasive tests of blood vessel function, cognitive testing, and a bone mineral density and body composition scan.
Receive payment of up to $125 for completing the main part of the study, plus some of your test results. Participation spans approximately two months.
timing: About 90 minutes for the consent/screening visit plus about 3.5 hours for the main study visit (two or three research visits total), with participation expected to span approximately two months.
